body:
Most flowers bloom in spring, and many leaves
change color in autumn. Due to global warming,
however, the timing of seasonal cycles is changing.
Scientists have been trying to find out exactly how
and where these cycles are changing, as well as
how fast the changes are occurring. The problem is
that it is impossible for them to keep track of
every single plant in the country. This is where
citizen science comes in. Project Budburst is a
program that engages citizens across the nation to
observe and record details about nearby plants.
Project Budburst can be easily accessed anywhere
you have an internet connection. (A) To get
involved, you first need to go through a simple
tutorial that helps you understand what to look for
when you observe a plant. (B) As you conduct your
observations, you will fill out a form to record the
plant’s location and track its changes throughout the
seasons. (C) You will record when it grows leaves,
flowers, and fruit, and when its leaves change color
and fall off in the autumn. (D) You can submit these
observation notes on the website or the app. (E)

the purpose of the Project Budburst programand its operation method
solution: 첫 번째 단락에서는 지구 온난화로 인해 식물의 계절 변화 시기가 달라지고 있으며, 과학자들이 이를 정확히 파악하려 하지만 모든 식물을 추적하는 것은 어렵다는 문제가 제시된다. 이를 해결하기 위한 방법으로 시민들이 참여하는 Project Budburst가 소개되고, 두 번째 단락에서는 이 프로그램의 참여 방법과 과정(튜토리얼 학습, 식물 선택, 관찰 및 기록)을 구체적으로 설명하고 있으므 로 이 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ❺ ‘Project Budburst 프 로그램의 목적과 그것의 운영 방식’이다.

How It Works
As a Feature Hunter participant, you will be
provided with a collection of images and ⓒasked

islands, volcanoes, or cities. You then examine the

crucial role in training and improving machine
learning models, which will automatically label raw
photographs with geographical features. Machine

aptitude assessment, Minho?
B: Yes, I did. I’m disappointed. I got a low score in
physical skills.
G: Don’t be discouraged. My teacher said this
assessment doesn’t decide your career.
B: I know, but I expected a higher score. I love
playing sports.

skills rather than on your weaker ones. Let me
see. Oh, you scored very high in interpersonal
skills.

reporter then?

Becoming the Best Possible Me
You are at a critical stage in your life, ⓐtrying to
figure out who you are and who you want to be.

being perfect. It is a journey ⓒto become the best

as you take your first steps.
For Those Struggling with Creativity
I’m a writer, and I love writing. But there are
moments when I feel anxious about my writing and
blame myself for (A)________________________. Creating
ⓓnew something is not easy, and you have
probably experienced this when you had difficulty
ⓔcoming up with ideas for group projects or
videos. So, how can we set aside those worries and
enjoy the creative process more?

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

an excessively vivid imagination
frequent errors in my writing
a constant lack of free time
a lack of creativity

I did some research on this issue and (A)고대 로마
인들은 ‘천재’를 오늘날 우리가 그것을 바라보는 방식
과 다르게 이해했다는 것을 알게 되었습니다. To

person but rather a divine assistant spirit of
creativity. They believed that geniuses lived in the

_________________________________. Everyone knew that

윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: they had no innate creativity at all
they were entirely responsible for it
their creative skills were not good enough
they didn't put enough effort into their work
they didn’t have to blame themselves entirely
solution: 고대 로마인들은 ‘genius(천재)’는 특별히 재능이 있는 사람이 아니라, 오히려 창의성의 신성한 보조 영혼을 가리키는 것이라 고 생각했고, 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서 모두가 genius 또한 작 품의 질에 책임이 있었다고 알고 있었다라고 언급하고 있으므 로, 예술가들의 작품이 만족스럽지 못하더라도 이것이 예술가 들만의 책임이 아니라고 보았다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은 ❺ ‘그들은 자신들을 전적으 로 탓할 필요가 없었다’이다.

body:
Some people may think this is not scientific, but
we often hear stories about how people get
inspired mysteriously. I once met an American poet
named Ruth Stone. Throughout her life, she worked
on a farm and wrote poems. She had a special way
of ⓐrecognizing when a poetic genius was coming
to her. She said it felt like the earth was shaking
under her feet! Whenever that feeling hit her, she
knew she had to return home quickly and write the
poem down before the genius found another poet.
My creative process isn’t as dramatic as hers. I
have to get up at the same time and work on my
laptop for hours every day. Yet, even in this rather
boring routine, I do get ideas coming from a
source I can’t ⓑidentify. Typically, it happens when
I’m deeply ⓒengaged in my work. Several hours or
even days can pass, and I completely ⓓimmerse
myself in my creative process. It’s at those moments
that
a
brilliant
idea
ⓔstrikes
me
somewhat
mysteriously. I’m sure that’s my genius.
Remember that you too have a magical genius
that is willing to help you. But first, you must put
your heart and soul into your work. Immerse yourself
in your work and try to enjoy the creative process
itself. If you do, your genius will come for sure.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
ⓐ: to accept or admit that something is true
ⓑ: to feel sympathy with someone or be able to
share their feelings
ⓒ: involved with something in an active and
interested way
ⓓ: to become or make somebody completely
involved in something
ⓔ: to suddenly think of a thought or an idea
solution: ⓐ ~을 알아차리다: 어떤 것이 사실임을 받아들이거나 인정하다 (→ to know who someone is or what something is, because you have seen, heard, experienced, or learned about them in the past(과거에 본 적이 있거나, 들었거나, 경험했거나, 배운 적이 있기 때문에 누가 누구인지, 또는 무엇이 무엇인지 알아보다)) ⓑ ~을 알아보다: 누군가에게 공감하거나 그들의 감정을 함께 느낄 수 있다(→ to recognize and correctly name someone or something(누군가나 무언가를 알아보고 정확하게 이름을 말하다))

Well, we are living examples of the Ship of

When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. I
played soccer every day, and I always thought that
I would grow up to become a great soccer player
one day. Forty years later, however, I don’t even
watch soccer games anymore. I’m actually a big fan
of American football now. My 12-year-old self may
find this a betrayal.
When I was 22, I graduated from college in India
with a computer science degree. At that time, it
never occurred to me that I would be living a
completely different life in the U.S. as a journalist
and podcast host. Thirty years ago, we didn’t even
have podcasts or smartphones, and the future was
not just unknown but unknowable.
When we look back, we can see how we have
changed, but when we look forward, we tend to
imagine ourselves as the same people, only older
and
taller.
That,
however,
is
not
the
case.
Biologically, our cells are continuously renewing
themselves,
and
our
brains
are
rewiring
and
modifying their connections. We are constantly
becoming new versions of ourselves.

윗글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: We must prepare thoroughly for an uncertain future.
Since the future is unknowable, worrying aboutit now is unnecessary.
We remain the same internally and physically,except for aging.
Unimaginable new technologies will appear anddramatically change our lives.
Our biological and mental states are constantlychanging.
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Have you heard of the “Ship of Theseus”? When
Theseus, a famous Greek hero, ⓐreturned from his
adventure of rescuing the children of Athens, the
Athenians wanted to preserve his ship. They kept
replacing the wood pieces that had decayed until
all the original pieces were replaced with new
ⓑone. In this situation, could we still call it the
Ship of Theseus?
Well, we are living examples of the Ship of
Theseus. Every day, we are changing and growing
to become new versions of ourselves. This means
that our future selves may be very different from
ⓒwho are we now. Then how can we create a future
we’ll be proud of? I have some advice for you.
First, actively envision the kind of person who you
want to become in the future. To do this, spend
time with different kinds of people to learn more
and stay curious. Second, when ⓓexpressing your
views online or with friends, remember that your
future self might disagree with your current opinions.
So, be respectful of other people’s opinions and
don’t just assume that you are always right. Finally,
your future self will have strengths and wisdom
ⓔthat you may lack today. Even if you can’t do
something now, you might be able to in the future.
So, don’t be afraid of new challenges. Be brave!

윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Why did the Athenians keep replacing the woodenpieces of the Ship of Theseus?
Why can a fully replaced ship still be calledTheseus’s ship?
What does the writer suggest doing to envisionthe kind of person you want to become?
Why should you be respectful of others‘ opinions?
What does the writer say about your future self’sstrengths and wisdom?

(A) To them, “genius” didn’t refer to a particularly

Some people may think this is not scientific, but
we often hear stories about how people get
inspired mysteriously. I once met an American poet
named Ruth Stone. Throughout her life, she worked
on a farm and wrote poems. She had a special way
of recognizing when a poetic genius was coming to
her. She said it felt like the earth was shaking
under her feet! Whenever that feeling hit her, she
knew ⓐ[what / that] she had to return home
quickly and write the poem down before the genius
found another poet.
My creative process isn’t as dramatic as hers. I
have to get up at the same time and work on my
laptop for hours every day. Yet, even in this rather
boring routine, I do get ideas that ⓑ[come /
coming] from a source I can’t identify. Typically, it
happens when I’m deeply engaged in my work.
Several hours or even days can pass, and I
completely immerse myself in my creative process.
It’s at those moments ⓒ[which / that] a brilliant
idea strikes me somewhat mysteriously. I’m sure
that’s my genius.
ⓓ여러분에게도 기꺼이 여러분을 도와줄 마법의
genius가 있다는 것을 기억하세요. But first, you must
put your heart and soul into your work. Immerse
yourself in your work and try to enjoy the creative
process itself. If you do, your genius will come for
sure.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

ⓐ            ⓑ
ⓒ
choices: thatcoming      that
thatcome      that
thatcome      which
whatcome      that
whatcoming      which
solution: ⓐ 완전한 절(she ~ another poet)을 이끌어 동사 knew의 목 적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다. ⓑ 선행사 ideas를 수식하는 관계사절의 동사 자리이므로, 선 행사에 수일치한 복수동사 come이 적절하다. ⓒ 주어 It이 가리키는 것이 없으며, it‘s 뒤에 쓰인 시간을 나 타내는 부사구 at those moments가 뒤에 이어지는 완전한 절 a ~ mysteriously에서 시간 수식어 역할을 하므로, 주어, 목적어, 또는 부사구를 강조할 때 쓰이는 ‘it ~ that … (…한 것은 바로 ~이다)’ 형태의 강조 구문이 쓰여야 하므로 that이 적절하다.

body:
I’m a writer, and I love writing. But there are
moments when I feel anxious about my writing and
blame myself for a lack of creativity. Creating
something new is not easy, and you have probably
experienced this when you had difficulty coming up
with ideas for group projects or videos. So, how
can we set aside those worries and enjoy the
creative process more?
I did some research on this issue and found that
ancient Romans understood “genius” differently from
how we see it today. To them, “genius” didn’t refer
to a particularly gifted person but rather a divine
assistant spirit of creativity. They believed that
geniuses lived in the walls of artists’ homes and
would come out and help them with their work.
This meant that if the artists’ work was not good
enough, they didn’t have to blame themselves
entirely. Everyone knew that their genius was also
responsible for the quality of the work.

윗글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: To gain creativity, we must look at things fromvarious perspectives.
When it is hard to solve a problem alone, thehelp of “genius” is needed.
A poor work can be seen as entirely theresponsibility of “genius”.
We should not criticize an artist just becausethe quality of their work is poor.
Seeing “genius” as a helpful spirit can lessenself-blame and make creativity more enjoyable.

I would grow up to become a great soccer player
one day. Forty years later, however, I don’t even
watch soccer games anymore. I’m actually a big fan

find this a betrayal.

with a computer science degree. At that time, it

and podcast host. Thirty years ago, we didn’t even
have podcasts or smartphones, and ______________

changed, but when we look forward, we tend to
imagine ourselves as the same people, only older
and

the

Feature Hunter
NASA has more than three million photos of Earth
ⓐtaking
from
space.
These
photos
can
be
invaluable to researchers in fields such as geology,
environmental science, and urban planning.
(A) In response to this challenge, a group of students
came up with the Feature Hunter project for
NASA. Participants of this project examine images
and label previously uncategorized photos for a
more comprehensive and searchable database.
(B) With such a vast amount of photographic data,
it can be challenging for scientists ⓑto search
for specific features and analyze them in detail.
(C) However, many of the photos are difficult to use
because they lack labels for common features
like islands, glaciers, volcanoes, and cities.
How It Works
As a Feature Hunter participant, you will be
ⓒprovided with a collection of images and asked
to identify specific features. You begin by selecting
the kind of feature you want to search for, such as
islands, volcanoes, or cities. You then examine the
displayed image and determine whether the feature
you are looking for ⓓis visible. If you can see the
feature in the image, select the Yes option. This will
bring you to a page ⓔwhich you will be asked to
identify the feature’s location by moving and
resizing the boxes around it. If you cannot see the
feature, or if it is not clear, click the No or Not
Sure option. Both of these options will contribute
to the creation of the best data possible.
How to Participate

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: NASA가 우주에서 촬영한 300만 장 이상의 지구 사진이 다양한 분야의 연구자들에게 매우 유용할 수 있다는 주어진 글 뒤에, However(그러나)를 사용하여 일반적인 지형에 대한 라벨이 없 어 많은 사진을 활용하기 어렵다는 상반된 내용을 설명하는 (C), (C)에서 언급된 라벨이 없는 방대한 양의 사진들을 such a vast amount of photographic data(그렇게 방대한 양의 사진 데이터)로 받아, 과학자들이 특정 지형을 찾아 자세히 분석하는 데 어려움을 겪을 수 있다는 내용을 설명하는 (B), (B)에서 언 급한 어려움을 this challenge(이러한 어려움)로 받아, 이를 해 결하기 위해 학생들이 NASA를 위한 Feature Hunter 프로젝트 를 고안했다는 내용을 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

Feature Hunter
NASA has more than three million photos of Earth
taken from space. These photos can be invaluable to
researchers in fields such as geology, environmental
science, and urban planning. However, many of the
photos are difficult (A)[to use / using] because they
lack
labels
for
common
features
like
islands,
glaciers, volcanoes, and cities. With such a vast
amount of photographic data, it can be challenging
for scientists (B)[to search / searching] for specific
features and analyze them in detail. In response to
this challenge, a group of students came up with
the Feature Hunter project for NASA. Participants of
this project examine images and label previously
uncategorized photos for a more comprehensive
and searchable database.
As a Feature Hunter participant, you will be
provided with a collection of images and asked to
identify specific features. You begin by selecting the
kind of feature you want to search for, such as
islands, volcanoes, or cities. You then examine the
displayed image and determine whether the feature
you are looking for is visible. If you can see the
feature in the image, select the Yes option. This will
bring you to a page (C)[on which / which] you will
be asked to identify the feature’s location by
moving and resizing the boxes around it. If you
cannot see the feature, or if it is not clear, click the
No or Not Sure option. Both of these options will
contribute to the creation of the best data possible.
The data gathered from Feature Hunter plays a
crucial role in training and improving machine
learning models, which will automatically label raw
photographs with geographical features. Machine
learning requires large sets of training data to
produce accurate results, and Feature Hunter users
can help develop this training data by simply
viewing images and identifying features. The more
data the citizen scientists label, the higher the
accuracy of the machine learning models can be.
Ultimately, this project will enhance the searchability
and usefulness of the images for both the scientific
community and the general public.

A common misconception in science is ⓐthat only
highly trained experts can participate in research
and
data
analysis.
However,
with
the
right
opportunity, anyone can become a scientist, and
yes, ⓑthat means even you! Dealing with a vast
amount of data can take scientists decades, but
with the eyes, ears, and perspectives of citizen
scientists, ⓒthis job can be completed in a few
years or even just a few months. Citizen scientists
collect, classify, or analyze data ⓓso that scientists
can use it for research. By making observations of
their surrounding environments or even by playing
a
simple
mobile
game,
they
can
help
the
professional scientific community expand knowledge
and ⓔspeed up new discoveries and innovations.

Feature Hunter
NASA has more than three million photos of Earth
taken from space. These photos can be invaluable to
researchers in fields such as geology, environmental
science, and urban planning. However, many of the
photos are difficult to use because they (A)[require
/ possess] labels for common features like islands,
glaciers, volcanoes, and cities. With such a vast
amount of photographic data, it can be challenging
for scientists to search for specific features and
analyze
them
in
detail.
In
response
to
this
challenge, a group of students came up with the
Feature Hunter project for NASA. Participants of this
project
examine
images
and
label
previously
uncategorized photos for a more (B)[inclusive /
partial] and searchable database.
Benefits and Outcomess
The data gathered from Feature Hunter plays a
crucial role in training and improving machine
learning models, which will automatically label raw
photographs with geographical features. Machine
learning requires large sets of training data to
produce accurate results, and Feature Hunter users
can help develop this training data by simply
viewing images and identifying features. The more

(A)

create something (A)[different / conventional].
Typically, the process of capturing a photograph
ends when the photographer presses the camera
button. However, Johansson’s photographs require
an additional process that “begins” after the
button is pressed. Let’s take a closer look at
one of his famous works, Go Your Own Road,
created in 2008. The two individual images may
not appear (B)[ordinary / extraordinary] on their
own, but when combined, they produce something
special. According to Johansson, there are three
simple rules to follow. The first rule is that the
photos you combine should be shot at the
same height and angle. Secondly, the combined
photos should have the same lighting. Finally,
the photos should be combined smoothly so
that it’s (C)[possible / impossible] to tell where
the different images begin and end.

Five sprinters were getting ready at the starting
line of the men’s 100-meter sprint in 1896 when
the first modern Olympic Games were ⓐheld. One
sprinter
in
particular
caught
the
spectators’
attention. He was touching the ground with his hips
ⓑraising towards the sky, while the others were
simply standing. The spectators laughed at the
position of his body, but it took only 11.8 seconds
for them to witness him ⓒsetting the first Olympic
record. This sprinter’s name was Thomas Burke, and
his innovative technique ⓓcalled a crouch start has
become the standard starting position since then.
Here are some key innovations introduced by great
athletes ⓔwho challenged themselves to find what
worked best. They proved that there is always room
for improvement.

body:
Ski jumping is one of the most spectacular winter
Olympic events. The skiers jump from the height of
90 meters, which is as high as a 30-story apartment
building. Most of the skiers are able to stay in the
air for about five to seven seconds. While they are
in the air, they are influenced by “lift,” an upward
force produced by air on a fast-moving object.
When the force of lift is balanced with the force of
gravity, the skiers can fly for long distances. The key
factors for them to increase lift and jumping distance
are increasing their speed, spreading out their
bodies and skis, and adjusting their body angle.
As jumps are judged mostly on jumping distance
as well as their style, skiers have tried many
techniques to maximize their time in the air, aiming
to achieve longer distances. In the beginning, most
skiers simply stood upright throughout their jump.
Later, this upright style was replaced by the
Kongsberger style. The skiers’ upper body was bent
at the hips, with their arms extended in front of
them and their skis parallel to each other. This
technique doubled the average jumping distance.
Everything changed in 1985, however, ⓐwhich
Swedish jumper Jan Boklöv introduced the V style.
In this style, the skiers position their skis into a “V”
shape with their heads ⓑplaced between the skis.
This modification increases the surface area and
creates more lift, leading to even greater jumping
distances. Wind tunnel tests showed that the V
style improves air lift by 28%, ⓒwhich means that
skiers can stay in the air longer. This style also
enables skiers to land at a safer speed, ⓓreduces
the risk of injury.
The V style was not immediately adopted by the
skiing community. In fact, it was initially ridiculed
and received fewer style points for breaking the
standard of parallel skis. However, the technique
proved so successful ⓔthat by 1992 all Olympic
medalists were using it.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the importance of understanding how bodyposition affects lift
the process of establishing standard ski jumpingstyles in the Olympics
improvement of records through advanced skiequipment and technology
innovative ski jumping techniques abandoneddue to conservative attitudes
constant efforts of ski jumpers to improveperformance through new jumping styles
solution: 스키 점프 선수들은 더 먼 거리를 뛰기 위해 the upright style, Kongsberger style 그리고 the V style과 같은 기술을 발전시 켜 왔으며, 처음에는 비판받았던 the V style이 결국 경기력을 향상시키며 1992년쯤에는 모든 올림픽 메달리스트들이 사용하 는 새로운 표준이 되었다는 것이 핵심 내용이므로 이 글의 주 제로 적절한 것은 ❺ ‘새로운 점프 방식들을 통해 경기력을 향 상시키려는 스키 점프 선수들의 지속적인 노력’이다. 동아(박용예) 5과

body:
[1]
Dick Fosbury practiced the major high jump
techniques, such as the scissors and the straddle,
for the Olympics when he was in high school. He
soon realized, however, that these techniques were
challenging for him because he didn’t (A)[possess /
lack] the strength or speed they require. Then he
found that when he went over the bar backward and
landed headfirst, he could jump higher than anyone
on his team. As an engineering major, he later
explained that arching the body backward keeps the
jumper’s center of gravity low to the ground. The
lower the center of gravity, the less energy required
to successfully jump over the bar. Another advantage
is that with this technique, there is less chance that
the jumper’s arms or legs will hit the bar and knock
it down. The result was a huge success. Fosbury won
a gold medal in the high jump in the 1968 Olympics.
But up to that point, every jumper in the event had
only gone over the bar forward, not backward.
Local newspapers (B)[complimented / mocked] his
style, saying that he looked like “a fish flopping in
a boat” and calling him “the world’s laziest high
jumper.” Eight years later, however, 90% of all high
jumpers were going over the bar backward just like
Fosbury. Today, every high jumper performs what is
known as the “Fosbury Flop.”
[2]
Athletes often face challenges when they realize
that conventional techniques aren’t working out for
them. They then make determined efforts to overcome
these weaknesses. Some of these athletes end up
developing remarkable innovative techniques, which
eventually
become
the
new
norm.
Innovation
(C)[thrives / withers] when individuals have a deep
understanding of themselves and discover their own
unique strengths.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)            (C)
choices: lackcomplimentedthrives
possessmockedwithers
lackmockedwithers
possesscomplimentedwithers
possessmockedthrives
solution: (A) 뒤에서 이런 기술들이 자신에게 어렵다는 것을 곧 깨달았다고 했으므로 그 기술들이 필요로 하는 힘이나 속도를 ‘가지지‘ 않았다 는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 possess(소유하다)가 적절하다. (B) 뒤에서 ‘배에서 퍼덕거리는 물고기’처럼 보인다고 말하고 그를 ‘세계에서 가장 게으른 높이뛰기 선수’라고 칭했다고 했으 므로 그의 스타일을 ‘조롱했다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 mocked(조롱했다)가 적절하다. (C) 운동선수들이 자신의 약점을 극복하기 위해 결연한 노력을 기울이고 이들 중 일부는 결국 주목할 만한 혁신적인 기술을 개발해 낸다고 했으므로, 개인이 자신에 대해 깊이 이해하고, 자신만의 고유한 강점을 발견할 때 혁신이 ‘번성하다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 thrives(번창하다)가 적절하다.

Up until the 1936 Olympics, swimmers used an
open turn. They touched the wall with one or two
hands first, turned to the side, and pushed off from
the wall by bending their legs. However, open turns
had the critical disadvantage of disrupting the
swimmers’ flow and speed.
This problem was resolved by an American high
school student named Al Vande Weghe. While
practicing the backstroke, he realized that his legs

to slow down. To overcome this drawback, he
devised a technique that is now known as a flip
turn. He would make a forward roll first to change
direction and then kick against the wall to speed
ahead. This technique allowed him to _______________

to take a risk and keep experimenting paid off.
Using this technique, he won a silver medal in the
1936 Olympics. Flip turns are now the standard in
freestyle and backstroke races.

The V Style in Ski Jumping
Ski jumping is one of the most spectacular winter
Olympic events. The skiers jump from the height of
90 meters, which is as high as a 30-story apartment
building. Most of the skiers are able to stay in the
air for about five to seven seconds. While they are
in the air, they are influenced by “lift,” an upward
force that (A)[is produced / produced] by air on a
fast-moving object. When the force of lift is
balanced with the force of gravity, the skiers can fly
for long distances. The key factors for them to
increase lift and jumping distance are increasing
their speed, spreading out their bodies and skis,
and adjusting their body ⓐangle.
As jumps are judged mostly on jumping distance
as well as their style, skiers have tried many
techniques to maximize their time in the air, aiming
to achieve ⓑlonger distances. In the beginning,
most skiers simply stood upright throughout their
jump. Later, this upright style was replaced by the
Kongsberger style. The skiers’ upper body was bent
at the hips, with their arms extended in front of
them and their skis parallel to each other. This
technique doubled the average jumping distance.
Everything
changed
in
1985,
however,
when
Swedish jumper Jan Boklöv introduced the V style.
In this style, the skiers position their skis into a “V”
shape with their heads placed between the skis.
This ⓒadjustment increases the surface area and
creates more lift, (B)[leads / leading] to even
greater
jumping
distances.
Wind
tunnel
tests
showed that the V style improves air lift by 28%,
which means that skiers can stay in the air longer.
This style also enables skiers to land at a safer
speed, ⓓreducing the risk of injury.
The V style was not immediately adopted by the
skiing community. In fact, it was initially ridiculed
and received fewer style points for ⓔfollowing the
standard of parallel skis. However, the technique
proved (C)[so / such] successful that by 1992 all
Olympic medalists were using it.

B: 정확해. 그것은 또한 평행 스키라는 기준을 깨뜨렸기 때문에 처음에는 더 적은 스타일 점수를 받았어. 그러나 풍동 실험들은 V 스타일이 양력을 증가시킨다는 것을 보여 주었고, 그 스타일은 (E)스키 선수들이 더 오래 공 중에 머무르고 더 안전하게 착지하도록 도왔어. 7) ⑤: 스키 점프 선수들은 더 먼 거리를 뛰기 위해 the upright style, Kongsberger style 그리고 the V style과 같은 기 술을 발전시켜 왔으며, 처음에는 비판받았던 the V style 이 결국 경기력을 향상시키며 1992년쯤에는 모든 올림 픽 메달리스트들이 사용하는 새로운 표준이 되었다는 것 이 핵심 내용이므로 이 글의 주제로 적절한 것은 ⑤ ‘새 로운 점프 방식들을 통해 경기력을 향상시키려는 스키 점프 선수들의 지속적인 노력’이다. 오답 ① 몸의 위치가 양력에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지 이해하 는 것의 중요성 ② 올림픽에서 표준 스키 점프 스타일을 확립하는 과정 ③ 첨단 스키 장비와 기술을 통한 기록의 향상 ④ 보수적인 태도 때문에 버려진 혁신적인 스키 점프 기 술들 8) ⑤: (A) 뒤에서 이런 기술들이 자신에게 어렵다는 것을 곧 깨달았다고 했으므로 그 기술들이 필요로 하는 힘이나 속도를 ‘가지지‘ 않았다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 possess(소유하다)가 적절하다. 본문변형 have → possess lack 부족하다 (B) 뒤에서 ‘배에서 퍼덕거리는 물고기’처럼 보인다고 말 하고 그를 ‘세계에서 가장 게으른 높이뛰기 선수’라고 칭했다고 했으므로 그의 스타일을 ‘조롱했다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 mocked(조롱했다)가 적절하다. 본문변형 criticized → mocked compliment 칭찬하다 (C) 운동선수들이 자신의 약점을 극복하기 위해 결연한 노력을 기울이고 이들 중 일부는 결국 주목할 만한 혁 신적인 기술을 개발해 낸다고 했으므로, 개인이 자신에 대해 깊이 이해하고, 자신만의 고유한 강점을 발견할 때 혁신이 ‘번성하다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 thrives (번창하다)가 적절하다. 본문변형 flourishes → thrives wither 약해지다 9) Dick Fosbury's revolutionary backward high jump technique and its lasting impact on the sport 제시문 Dick Fosbury의 혁신적인 뒤로 넘는 높이뛰기 기술 과 그것이 스포츠에 끼친 지속적인 영향 10) ⑤: 오픈 턴이 수영 선수들의 흐름과 속도에 지장을 준다는 결정적인 단점이 있지만, 이 문제는 Al Vande Weghe에 의해 해결되었다고 언급되었으며, 그가 오픈 턴을 할 때 자신의 다리가 너무 무겁고 속도가 늦어지게 되는 단점 을 극복하기 위해, 플립 턴을 고안했다는 내용이 이어지 므로, 이 새로운 기술로 턴을 하는 동안 오픈 턴과 달리 흐름과 속도에 지장을 주지 않는 빈칸에 내용이 들어가 야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ⑤ ‘턴을 하는 동안 그의 속도를 유지하다‘이다. 오답 ① 그의 팔과 다리에 느껴지는 무게감을 제거하다 ② 그의 동작을 느리게 함으로써 저항을 줄이다 ③ 그의 상체 힘을 최대한 활용하다 ④ 턴을 하는 동안 적절한 호흡에 집중하다 11) ③: (A) 콤마(,) 앞에 절 전체(the V style ~ 28%)에 대한 부 연 설명을 하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 절 전체가 선행 사일 때 단수 취급하므로 단수동사 means가 적절하다. (B) ‘동사 enables+목적어 skiers+목적격보어(…가 ~하 게 하다[~하는 것을 가능하게 하다)]’의 구조로 쓰이는 동사 enable은, to부정사를 목적격보어로 취하는 동사 이므로 to land가 적절하다. (C) 등위 접속사 and로 과거동사 was와 병렬을 이루는 두 번째 동사로, 주어 it(=The V style)가 더 적은 스타 일 점수를 ‘받은’ 주체이자 뒤에 목적어가 이어지므로, 과거동사 received가 적절하다. 12) lift, jumping distances, safer, standard 요약문 1985년에 Jan Boklöv에 의해 도입된 V 스타일은 표면적을 넓혀 양력을 증가시켰고, 이는 점프 거리를 늘리 는 데 도움을 주었고 더 안전한 착지를 가능하게 했으며, 초기의 비판에도 불구하고 그것은 1992년까지 모든 올림픽 메달리스트들이 사용하는 표준 기술이 되었다. 13) ⑤: 대부분의 스키 점프 선수들은 약 5초에서 7초 동안 공 중에 머물 수 있다고 했지만 얼마나 멀리 날 수 있는지는 언급되지 않았으므로 ⑤ ‘대부분의 스키 점프 선수들은 얼마나 멀리 날 수 있는가?‘는 답할 수 없는 질문이다. 오답 ① 스키 점프 경기에서 선수들은 어느 높이에서 점프하 는가? (→그들은 약 90미터 높이에서 점프하며, 이는 30층 아파트 건물 높이와 같다.) ② ‘양력(lift)’이란 무엇이며, 그것은 공중에 있는 스키 점프 선수들에게 어떤 영향을 미치는가? (→양력은 빠 르게 움직이는 물체에 공기가 만들어내는 위로 향하는 힘이며, 선수들이 더 오래 공중에 머물고 더 멀리 날 수 있도록 도와준다.) ③ 어떤 요소들이 스키 점프 선수들이 양력을 증가시키 고 더 멀리 뛰는 데 도움을 주는가? (→속도를 높이고, 몸과 스키를 넓게 펼치며, 몸의 각도를 조절하는 것이 양력과 점프 거리를 증가시키는 데 도움이 된다.) ④ Kongsberger 스타일은 이전의 직립 자세와 어떻게 달랐는가? (→Kongsberger 스타일에서는 선수들이 상 체를 앞으로 굽히고 팔을 앞쪽으로 뻗으며 스키를 평행 하게 유지했다는 점에서, 몸을 곧게 세웠던 이전 자세 와 달랐다.) 14) ①: 주어진 문장은 ‘그러나 그에게는 이러한 기술들이 필요 로 하는 힘이나 속도가 없었기 때문에 자신에게 이런 기술들이 어렵다는 것을 곧 깨달았다.’라는 뜻으로 However(그러나)로 시작하고 these techniques(이러한 기술들)와 관련한 내용이 언급되고 있으므로, 이 문장 앞에는 먼저 해당 기술들(these techniques)이 제시되어 야 하며, 흐름이 전환되는 부분을 찾아야 한다. (A) 앞 에서는 Dick Fosbury가 가위뛰기와 스트래들과 같은 주 요 높이뛰기 기술을 연습했다고 설명하고 있는데, 여기 서 언급된 가위뛰기와 스트래들이 바로 주어진 문장의 these techniques에 해당하며, (A) 뒤에는 바를 뒤로 넘 는 새로운 방식을 발견하여 더 높이 뛸 수 있었다는 내 용이 이어져 흐름이 전환되고 있으므로, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (A)이다. 15) ④: 포스베리 플롭은 바를 뒤로 넘어 머리부터 떨어지는 기술 이므로 ⓓ ‘바를 앞으로 넘기’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다. 제시문 플립 턴 포스베리 플롭 전통적인 기술 오픈 턴 가위뛰기와 스트래들 방식 확인된 한계 ⓐ무거운 다리가 흐름과 속도를 방해함 ⓑ요구되는 힘과 속도가 부족함 개발된 새로운 기술 ⓒ앞구르기와 벽을 발로 밀치고 나가기 ⓓ바를 앞으로 (→뒤로) 넘기 결과 속도와 추진력을 유지함 ⓔ무게 중심을 낮게 유지함으로써 더 높이 점프하기 주요 성취 1936년 올림픽 은메달 1968년 올림픽 금메달 현재 자유형과 배영 에서의 세계적인 표준 턴 높이뛰기 선수들 사이의 일반적인 기술 16) ⑤: ⓔ following(따르는) → breaking(깨뜨리는) 본문변형 ⓒ modification → adjustment 17) ④: (A) 선행사 an upward force를 수식하는 관계사절의 동 사 자리이며, an upward force가 공기에 의해 ‘만들어 진’ 대상이므로 동사형 수동태(be+p.p.) is produced가 적절하다. 본문변형 an upward force produced by air → an upward force that is produced by air (B) 완전한 절(This ~ lift)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연 결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이다. 따라서 현 재분사 leading이 적절하다. (C) 뒤에 형용사 successful을 수식하고 있으며 접속사 that과 함께 ‘so+형용사+that절(매우 ~해서 (그 결과) …하다)’의 구문을 이루어야 하므로 형용사를 수식할 수 있는 부사 so가 적절하다. 참고로 such는 명사(구)를 수 식한다. 18) ⓐ when they realize that conventional techniques aren’t working out for them 또는 when they realize conventional techniques aren’t working out for them ⓑ which eventually become the new norm : ⓐ 완전한 절(conventional ~ them)을 이끌어 동사 realize 의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌어야 하므로 what 을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고치거나, 목적어절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사는 생략 가능하므로 what을 삭제한다. *원래 지문에서는 that이 쓰였음 ⓑ 선행사 remarkable innovative techniques를 부연 설명 하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, 주격 관계대명사가 이끄는 관계사절의 동사는 선행사에 수일치하며 remarkable innovative techniques가 복수명사구이므로 단수동사 becomes를 복수동사 become으로 고친다. 19) While practicing the backstroke, he realized that his legs were too heavy for an open turn, which caused him to slow down. : • ‘배영을 연습하던 중‘을 영작하기 위해 접속사 While 뒤 에 분사구문을 써야 하며, 의미상 주어인 he가 배영을 ’연 습하는‘ 주체이므로 동사원형 practice를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 practicing로 변형하여 이어 쓴다. • ’그는 자신의 다리가 오픈 턴을 하기에 너무 무겁다는 것을 깨달았다’를 영작하기 위해 주어 he, 동사 realized 뒤에 목적어절을 쓰기 위해 명사절 접속사 that을 이어 쓴다. that 뒤에 that절의 주어 his legs, 동사 were, 주격 보어 too heavy, 수식어구 for an open turn을 차례대로 쓴다. • ‘이것이 그를 느려지게 한다’를 영작하기 위해 콤마(,) 뒤에 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which를 쓰고 동사 cause는 ‘cause+목적어+to부정사(목적격보어)(…가 ~하도 록 유발하다[야기하다])’의 5형식 구조로 쓰이므로 동사 caused, 목적어 him, 목적격보어 to slow down을 차례대 로 쓴다. 20) ②: (A) 다음 문장에서 이 기술은 평균 점프 거리를 두 배 로 늘렸다고 했으므로 양력과 점프 거리를 증가시키는 자세가 언급되는 것이 자연스럽다. 앞 문단에서 양력과 점프 거리를 증가시키는 핵심 요소는 몸과 스키를 펼 치는 것이라고 했으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 reached out(뻗은), stretched(쭉 편), extended(뻗 은)가 적절하다. *원래 지문에서는 extended(뻗은)가 쓰였음 (B) 이러한 변형(V자 스타일)은 표면적을 넓힌다고 했고, 이것이 결과적으로 더 긴 비행거리로 이어진다고 했으 므로 더 많은 양력을 만들어낸다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 generates(발생 시키다), produces(만들다), creates(만들다)가 적절하다. *원래 지문에서는 creates(만들다)가 쓰였음 오답 ① 굽힌 발생시키다 ③ 쭉 편 약화시키다 ④ 뻗은 저해하다 ⑤ 접은 만들다

G: Hey, Paul. Take a look at this.
B: Why is that man standing knee-deep in water?
G: He’s the foreign minister of Tuvalu, an island country
in the Pacific Ocean. He’s giving a speech to
demonstrate that his country is sinking because of
global warming. The area where he’s standing
used to be land.
B: That’s terrible! _______________________________ things
were getting this bad.
G: He said that about 40 percent of the capital
district is underwater at high tides already. If
sea levels keep rising, the whole country will be
underwater by the end of the century.
B: Oh, no! We should take action. Can you send
me the link to the news article so I can let
more people know about the situation?
G: Sure. I’ll send it to you right away.

위 대화의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞지 않은 것은?
choices: I didn’t have a clue that
I knew nothing that
I was unaware that
I had no idea that
I was certain that
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

Over the past two centuries, human activities
ⓐhave generated a significant amount of carbon
dioxide, commonly referred to as CO₂. This gas
itself is not dangerous when we encounter it in
everyday situations. (A)____________, excessive amounts
of this gas in the atmosphere have contributed to
the greenhouse effect, ⓑresult in a gradual increase
in the Earth’s surface temperature. To make matters
worse, this increase has sped up in recent years
and is seriously threatening life on our planet. We
must act immediately to stop any further climate
change.
While many high-tech solutions such as carbon
capture have ⓒbeen proposed, they are often too
expensive to ⓓbe used widely. (B)____________, there
are also low-tech, economical, and even long-lasting
solutions available. In this report, we will focus on
one of the most powerful nature-based solutions to
climate change: whales, the giant helpers ⓔliving
under the sea.

body:
Whales are amazing creatures. They are enormous
and live incredibly long lives. The largest blue
whales can grow as long as 30 meters and weigh
over 200 tons, and some whales have been known
to live for more than 100 years. These giants do
extremely beneficial things for the environment
throughout their long lives and even after death.
According to scientists, a single whale can absorb
about 550 kilograms of CO₂ per year, while a tree
can absorb only 22.
Moreover, after they die, whales sink to the ocean
floor with all the CO₂ they absorbed during their
lives. Their bodies then become food and habitats
for deep-sea creatures. This process is called a
whale fall. Whale falls permanently bury about
145,000 tons of CO₂ under the sea every year. This
achievement is basically what expensive carbon
capture technologies aim to do — capture carbon
and then store it underground.

CO₂ through whale falls, whales also make a
significant indirect contribution to reducing CO₂
through an act called a whale pump. This refers to
the vertical movements of whales that help circulate
nutrients across different depths of the ocean.
Whales dive deep into the ocean to feed on prey
such as krill and small fish, and they occasionally
swim up to the surface to breathe. When they near
the surface, they release an enormous amount of
waste. This waste is rich in nutrients that are
essential for creatures living in that area. Specifically,
it creates the perfect growing conditions for some
microscopic creatures floating at the surface of the
ocean.
These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look
tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they
____________________________________. They absorb about
40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and produce
about 50% of the atmosphere’s oxygen. They do
this through photosynthesis, a process that creates
energy
using
carbon,
water,
and
light.
It
is
estimated that increasing the world’s phytoplankton
by 1% is equivalent to planting 2 billion new trees.
Whale pumps deliver nutrients not only to the
ocean surface but also to deeper areas of the
ocean. As whales swim back down to feed at the
ocean’s bottom, their movements stir up the water
and bring nutrients down to the creatures living
below. Whale pumps promote the growth of marine
life at various depths throughout the ocean.

body:
I’m a writer, and I love writing. But there are
moments when I feel anxious about my writing and
blame myself for a lack of creativity. Creating
something new is not easy, and you have probably
experienced this when you had difficulty coming up
with ideas for group projects or videos. So, how
can we set aside those worries and enjoy the
creative process more?
I did some research on this issue and found that
ancient Romans understood “genius” differently from
how we see ⓐit today. To ⓑthem, “genius” didn’t
refer to a particularly gifted person but rather a
divine assistant spirit of creativity. ⓒThey believed
that geniuses lived in the walls of artists’ homes and
would come out and help them with their work.
This meant that if the artists’ work was not good
enough, they didn’t have to blame ⓓthemselves
entirely. Everyone knew that ⓔtheir genius was also
responsible for the quality of the work.

ⓒ: artists
ⓓ: artists
ⓔ: artists

When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. I
played soccer every day, and I always thought that
I would grow up to become a great soccer player
one day.
(A) At that time, it never occurred to me that I
would be living a completely different life in
the U.S. as a journalist and podcast host. Thirty
years ago, we didn’t even have podcasts or
smartphones, and the future was not just
unknown but unknowable.
(B) My 12-year-old self may find this a betrayal.
When I was 22, I graduated from college in
India with a computer science degree.
(C) Forty years later, however, I don’t even watch
soccer games anymore. I’m actually a big fan of
American football now.
When we look back, we can see how we have
changed, but when we look forward, we tend to
imagine ourselves as the same people, only older
and
taller.
That,
however,
is
not
the
case.
Biologically, our cells are continuously renewing
themselves,
and
our
brains
are
rewiring
and
modifying their connections. We are constantly
becoming new versions of ourselves.

고쳐야 한다. 그 외, isn't 뒤에 이어지는 주격보어로 형용사의 원급 dramatic이 as 사이에 위치한 것은 알맞다. ⓑ 완전한 절(you too ~ you)을 이끌어 동사 Remember의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명 사절 접속사 that으로 고쳐야 한다. 그 외, 동사원형 Remember로 시작하는 명령문은 알맞으며, 주어가 없는 불 완전한 절(is ~ you)을 이끌어 선행사 a magical genius를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루는 주격 관계대명사 that 또한 적절하다. 7) ②: 다음 문장에서 ‘자신의 일에 몰입하고 창작 과정 자체를 즐기려고 노력해 보세요.’라고 했으므로 흐름상 빈칸에 영어I 동아(박용예) 1과 예상문제 2회 - 주관식(서답형) 5. I do get ideas coming from a source I can’t identify 6. ⓐ My creative process isn’t as dramatic as hers. ⓑ Remember that you too have a magical genius that is willing to help you. 12. trying to figure out who you are and who you want to be 16. the mysterious process of receiving creative ideas 19. (1) could still call it the Ship of Theseus (2) your future self might disagree with your current opinions 20. (A) genius (B) immerse (C) enjoy 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ② ‘자신의 일에 심혈을 기울 이다’이다. 오답 ① 가만히 앉아 있지 말고 몸을 이리저리 움직이다 ③ 비록 즐겁지 않더라도 계속 집중하다 ④ 주변 사람들에게 도움을 요청하다 ⑤ 긴장을 풀고 차분하게 지내다 8) ④: (A) 전치사 For의 목적어 Those를 수식하는 분사 자리이 므로, 현재분사 Worrying이 적절하다. (B) 완전한 절(I would ~ one day)을 이끌어 동사 thought의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므 로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다. (C) 완전한 절(I ~ podcast host)을 이끌어 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어를 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that 은 적절하다. 9) ④, ⑤ : ⓓ remembering → remember (접속사가 남아 있는 분사 구문(when expressing ~ with friends)에 이어지는 주절에 서, 접속사 that이 목적어 역할을 하는 완전한 절(your future self ~ current opinions)을 이끌고 있을 뿐 주절의 동사가 없으므로, 동사원형으로 시작하는 명령문이 되도록 remembering을 remember로 고친다.) ⓔ which → that (완전한 절(you ~ right)을 이끌어 동사 assume의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 which를 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.) 오답 ⓐ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(had decayed)을 이끌어 선행 사 the wood pieces를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으 므로 주격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다. ⓑ 접속사 until이 이끄는 시간 부사절의 주어 all the original pieces에 이어지는 동사 자리로, all the original pieces가 ‘교체되는’ 대상이므로 복수로 수일치한 수동태 were replaced는 적절하다. ⓒ 전치사 of의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we’ll ~ of)을 이끌어 선행사 a future를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있 으므로 목적격 관계대명사 that은 적절하다. 10) ②: 주어진 문장은 ‘이는 곧 미래의 우리 모습이 지금의 우 리 모습과 매우 다를 수 있음을 의미합니다.’라는 뜻으로 ‘미래의 우리 모습이 지금의 우리 모습과 매우 다를 수 있는 상황’과 같은 상황이 주어진 문장 앞에 언급되어야 한다. (B) 앞 문장에서 우리가 매일 변화하고 성장하여 새로운 버전이 되고 있다고 했는데, 이것이 바로 주어진 문장에서 언급한 지금의 우리 모습과 미래의 우리 모습 이 매우 다를 수 있는 상황을 가리킨다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 들어갈 곳으로 가장 적절한 것은 (B)이다. 11) ⑤: 미래의 여러분에게는 현재 여러분이 부족할 수 있는 강 점과 지혜가 있을 것이며, 지금 무언가를 할 수 없더라 도 미래에는 할 수 있을지도 모른다고 언급되었으므로 ⑤ ‘당신이 지금 강점과 지혜를 갖고 있지 않다면, 미래에 도 그것들을 가질 수 없을 것이다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용 이다. 오답 ① 아테네 사람들은 테세우스의 배를 보존하기 위해 그 것을 계속 수리했다. ② 우리는 지금도 끊임없이 새로운 버전의 자신으로 변 화하고 있는 중이다. ③ 미래에 당신이 원하는 사람이 되기 위해서는 다양한 사람들을 만나는 것이 바람직하다. ④ 현재의 당신의 생각은 과거의 당신의 생각과 다를 수 있다. 12) trying to figure out who you are and who you want to be : • <조건>에 맞게 완전한 절(You ~ life)에 이어지는 분사 구문으로, 주절의 주어 You가 ‘노력하는’ 주체이므로 능동 을 나타내는 현재분사 trying이 쓰였으며, ‘~하려고 노력 하다’라는 뜻을 나타낼 때 ‘try+to부정사‘를 사용하므로 trying의 목적어로 to부정사구 to figure out을 영작한다. • 간접의문문을 사용해야 하므로 의문사 who를 사용하여 ’의문사+주어+동사‘의 어순으로 who you are(여러분이 누구인지)와 who you want to be(여러분은 누가 되기를 원하는지)를 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결하여 이어 쓴다. 13) ③: ⓒ가 가리키는 것은 ancient Romans이다. 14) ⑤: 글쓴이는 창작 과정에서 아이디어가 떠오르지 않을 때 스스로를 자책하며 불안해하지만, 천재성을 개인이 아 닌 '외부의 조력자(신성한 영혼)'로 여겼던 고대 로마인 들의 지혜를 통해 창작의 결과에 대한 심리적 부담을 나누고 과정을 더 즐길 수 있다는 것이 글의 핵심 내 용이므로 이 글의 제목으로 적절한 것은 ⑤ ‘창작의 불 안을 극복하기 위해 고대 지혜로부터 배우기’이다. 오답 ① 창의적인 아이디어의 강력한 원천으로서의 불안 ② 고대 로마인들의 놀라운 창의성 ③ 고대 로마 예술가들의 독특한 창작 과정 ④ 창작의 실패에 대한 책임을 genius에게 전가하기 15) ③: (A) how가 이끄는 절의 동사 get의 보어 자리로 주어 people이 영감을 ‘받는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미인 과 거분사 inspired가 적절하다. (B) be동사의 부정형 isn't의 보어 자리이므로 형용사 dramatic이 적절하다. (C) 명사 routine을 수식하는 분사 자리로, routine은 사 람이 아니므로 지루함을 느끼는 대상이 아니라, 지루하 게 ‘만드는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 boring 이 적절하다. 16) the mysterious process of receiving creative ideas 제시문 창의적인 아이디어를 얻는 신비로운 과정 17) ⑤: 축구에 매우 열정적이었고 나중에 축구선수가 될 거라 고 생각했다는 주어진 글 뒤에 however(그러나)로 연결 하여 40년 후에 더 이상 축구 경기를 보지도 않는다는 상반된 내용이 이어지는 (C), 축구 대신 미식축구의 열 렬한 팬이라고 이어서 설명한 뒤 이러한 사실을 this로 이어받아 12살의 자신이 this(지금은 축구 대신 미식축 구의 팬이라는 것)를 배신이라고 여길지도 모른다고 언 급한 (B), 22살에 인도에서 컴퓨터 공학 학위를 받고 대학을 졸업했고, 그 시절을 At that time(그 당시에는) 으로 이어받아 그 당시에는 현재와 다른 삶을 살고 있 을 것으로 생각하지 못했다고 언급하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 18) ①: 과거의 내가 예상치 못할 정도로 취향, 진로, 생각이 시 간이 지나며 크게 변할 수 있다는 것을 보여주는 첫 번 째 문단의 예시에 이어, 우리는 흔히 미래의 자신을 나 이가 더 든 똑같은 사람으로 상상하지만, 실제로는 생 물학적으로도 끊임없이 새로운 세포로 바꿔가며 새로운 버전의 자신이 되어 간다는 두 번째 문단으로 이어지므 로, 이 글의 주제로 적절한 것은 ① ‘내적으로도 신체적 으로도 끊임없이 변화하는 우리 자신’이 알맞다. 오답 ② 현재의 직업으로 바로 이어지는 어릴 적 관심 ③ 기술 발전이 우리의 미래에 미치는 영향 ④ 과거의 나와 현재의 내가 다른 이유들 ⑤ 미래에 전망 좋은 직업 선택지들 19) (1) could still call it the Ship of Theseus (2) your future self might disagree with your current opinions 질문 (1) 배의 모든 원래 부품들이 교체되었을 때 어떤 질문이 제기되는가? → 그 질문은 우리가 그것을 여전히 테세우스의 배라고 부 를 수 있는지이다. (2) 당신의 견해를 표현할 때 왜 다른 사람들의 의견을 존 중해야 하는가? → 왜냐하면 미래의 당신이 현재의 당신 의견에 동의하지 않을지도 모르기 때문이다. 20) (A) genius (B) immerse (C) enjoy 요약문 시인 Ruth Stone의 극적인 영감과 그의 창의적 과 정을 통해, 글쓴이는 (A)천재성이 자신의 일에 완전히 (B)몰 입하고 진정으로 그 과정을 (C)즐기는 사람들에게 반드시 찾아올 것이라고 조언한다. 21) ①: 앞 절과 접속사 but으로 연결되어 있으므로 과거를 돌 아볼 때 우리가 어떻게 변했는지 알 수 있다는 내용과 대조되어야 하며, 뒤에 또 다시 however로 이어져 빈 칸에 들어갈 내용이 사실이 아니며 생물학적으로 세포 가 계속 새롭게 바뀌고 있다고 언급되고 있으므로, 미 래를 내다볼 때는 ‘변화가 없을 것’이라 상상하는 경향 이 있다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ① ‘단지 나이가 더 들고 키만 더 큰, 똑같은 사람’이다. 오답 ② 현재의 우리와는 다른 개인들 ③ 그들의 미래가 명확하게 예측될 수 있는 사람들 ④ 우리가 바라는 대로 미래를 통제할 수 있는 사람들 ⑤ 우리의 과거 기억 속에 영원히 갇혀 있는 사람들 22) ⑤: (A) 앞에서 필자가 자신의 글쓰기에 불안해하며, 뒤에서 무언가를 새로 만드는 것은 쉽지 않다고 했으므로 자신 의 창의성 ‘부족’에 대해 스스로를 비난한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 lack(부족)이 적절하다. abundance 풍족함 (B) 뒤에서 고대 로마인들은 ‘genius’를 개인의 뛰어난 재능이 아닌 외부의 창의적 존재로 이해했고, 예술가들 이 자신의 작품이 만족스럽지 못하더라도 그들의 genius 또한 작품의 질에 책임이 있다는 것을 알고 있었다고 했 으므로 고대 로마인들이 ‘genius’를 바라보는 방식이 오 늘날 우리의 방식과 ‘다르다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라 서 differently from(~와는 다르게)이 적절하다. similarly to ~ ~와 비슷하게 (C) 고대 로마인들은 ‘genius(천재)’를 특별히 재능이 있 는 사람이 아니라, 창의성의 신성한 보조 영혼으로 이해 했고, 그들의 genius 또한 작품의 질에 책임이 있다는 것을 알고 있었다고 했으므로 예술가들의 작품이 만족 스럽지 못하더라도 자기 자신을 ‘전적으로’ 탓하지 않아 도 되었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 entirely(전적으 로)가 적절하다. partially 부분적으로

B: How was your weekend, Yerin?
G: I went to Erik Johansson’s exhibition, and it was
fantastic.
B: Oh, tell me more about it.
G: The artist created his artwork by doing some
extra work on the photos he took.
B: That’s interesting. What was your favorite piece?
G: I found the work (A)[titled / was titled] LandFall
most impressive. It depicts a house (B)[what /
that] is just about to fall off a cliff.
B: How is that possible?
G: He combined images of real landscapes and a
model he made with boxes, with liquid (C)[run /
running] down it.
B: Impressive! Did you use the audio guide?
G: No, I didn’t. But there was a revealing video
about his creative process.
B: I’ll have to check it out as well.

위 대화의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: was titled   whatrun
was titled   thatrunning
titled   thatrunning
titled   whatrunning
titled   thatrun
solution: (A) ‘…가 ~함을 발견하다’의 의미로 'find+목적어+목적격보어 (most impressive)‘의 구조를 갖는 동사 found의 목적어 the work 를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, the work가 LandFall라고 ‘제목이 지어진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 titled가 적절하다. (B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is ~ cliff)을 이끌어 선행사 a house를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명 사 that이 적절하다. (C) 전치사 with, 명사 liquid에 이어지는 분사 자리로 ‘~가 … 하면서, ~가 …한 채로’라는 의미를 갖는 ‘with 분사구문(with+ 명사(구)+분사(-ing/p.p.))’으로, 앞의 명사(구)와 능동 관계를 이 루면 현재분사를 쓰고, 수동 관계를 이루면 과거분사를 쓴다. 명사 liquid(액체)는 ‘흘러내리는’ 주체이며, run은 자동사로 수 동의 의미로 쓰이지 않으므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 running이 적절하다.

Everything
changed
in
1985,
however,
when
Swedish jumper Jan Boklöv introduced the V style.
In this style, the skiers position their skis into a “V”
shape with their heads ⓐplaced between the skis.
This modification increases the surface area and
creates more lift, ⓑleading to even greater jumping
distances. Wind tunnel tests showed that the V
style improves air lift by 28%, which means ⓒthat
skiers can stay in the air longer. This style also
enables skiers ⓓland at a safer speed, reducing the
risk of injury.
The V style was not immediately adopted by the
skiing community. In fact, it was initially ridiculed
and received fewer style points for breaking the
standard of parallel skis. However, the technique
proved so ⓔsuccessful that by 1992 all Olympic
medalists were using it.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: scientific explanations of air resistance in wintersports
the beginning of a revolutionary new ski jumpingstyle
biased scoring systems regarding jumping stylesin the Olympics

body:
Up until the 1936 Olympics, swimmers used an
open turn. They touched the wall with one or two
hands first, turned to the side, and pushed off from
the wall by bending their legs. However, open turns
had the critical disadvantage of disrupting the
swimmers’ flow and speed.
This problem was resolved by an American high
school student named Al Vande Weghe. While
(A)[practicing / practiced] the backstroke, he realized
that his legs were too heavy for an open turn,
which caused him (B)[slowing / to slow] down. To
overcome this drawback, he devised a technique
that is now known as a flip turn. He would make a
forward roll first to change direction and then kick
against the wall to speed ahead. This technique
allowed him to maintain as much of his speed and
momentum as possible. His willingness to take a
risk and keep experimenting paid off. (C)[Used /
Using] this technique, he won a silver medal in the
1936 Olympics. Flip turns are now the standard in
freestyle and backstroke races.

선수 들이 경기력을 향상시키는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.’는 양 력을 늘리기 위한 핵심 요소인 자세나 기술 변화와 관 련된 설명이 아니라 체중 에 관한 언급으로, 앞뒤 흐름 과 직접적으로 연결되지 않는다. 따라서 (A)는 글의 흐 름과 관련 없다. 15) ⑤: (A) 뒤에서 이는 선수들이 공중에 더 오래 머무를 수 있음을 의미한다고 했으므로 V 스타일이 공기 양력을 28% ‘향상시킨다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 improves(향상시키다), increases(증가시키다), refines(개선하다)이다. *원래 지문에서는 improves(향상시키다)가 쓰였음 (B) 뒤에서 처음에는 평행 스키의 표준을 깼다는 이유 로 V 스타일은 조롱을 받고 더 적은 스타일 점수를 받 았다고 했으므로 V 스타일은 스키 사회에서 즉각 ’받 아들여지지’ 않았다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸 에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 embraced(받아들여진), accepted(받아들여진), adopted(채택된)가 적절하다. *원래 지문에서는 adopted(채택된)가 쓰였음 오답 ① 향상시키다 거부된 ② 감소시키다 받아들여진 ③ 악화시키다 채택된 ④ 증가시키다 묵살된 16) This style also enables skiers to land at a safer speed, reducing the risk of injury. : • ‘이 스타일은 또한 선수들이 더 안전한 속도로 착지하 는 것을 가능하게 한다’를 영작하기 위해 ‘enable+목적어 +목적격보어(to부정사)(…가 ~하는 것을 가능하게 하다)’ 를 사용한다. 주어 This style에 수일치한 단수 동사구 also enables를 쓰고, 목적어 skiers에 이어지는 to부정사 구 to land와 ‘더 안전한 속도로’를 뜻하는 전치사구 at a safer speed를 차례대로 쓴다. • 접속사 없이 동사구가 바로 완전한 절에 이어질 수 없 으므로 분사구문의 형태가 되어야 하며, 주절의 주어 This style가 ‘줄이는‘ 주체이므로, 콤마(,) 뒤에 동사 reduce를 현재분사 reducing으로 변형하고 목적어 the risk of injury를 차례대로 써서 분사구문을 완성한다. 17) ③: Dick Fosbury는 기존의 높이뛰기 기술들인 가위뛰기와 스트래들에 필요한 힘이나 속도가 부족해 어려움을 겪 었지만, 무게 중심을 지면에 낮게 유지할 수 있도록 해 주는 뒤로 넘는 기술로 더 높이 뛸 수 있었다고 했으 므로, 무게 중심이 낮을수록 더 높이 뛰는 데 필요한 힘이나 속도가 더 적게 든다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따 라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ③ ‘바를 성공적 으로 뛰어넘는 데 필요한 에너지가 더 줄어든다.’이다. 오답 ① 높이뛰기 선수가 다리로 바를 건드릴 가능성이 더 높아진다. ② 몸의 회전을 통제하는 것이 더 어려워진다. ④ 점프 동안 균형을 잃을 위험이 더 높아진다. ⑤ 바를 넘기 위해 더 많은 에너지가 필요하다. 18) ②: ⓑ 주격 관계대명사는 단독으로 생략 할 수 없으며, ‘주 격 관계대명사+be동사‘의 형태로 생략 가능하므로 who was를 함께 생략해야 한다. 19) ②: Dick Fosbury는 올림픽을 위해 가위뛰기와 스트래들과 같은 주요 높이뛰기 기술을 연습했다는 주어진 글 뒤에 However(그러나)로 시작하여, 앞서 언급된 가위뛰기와 스트래들을 these techniques(이러한 기술들)로 이어받 아 자신의 신체적 한계로 인해 이런 기술들이 어렵다는 것을 곧 깨달았다는 상반된 내용의 (B), (B)의 마지막 문 장에서 기존 기술이 어렵다는 것을 깨닫고, 등을 뒤로 해서 넘는 새로운 방식을 발견했다고 언급한 뒤 이 새 로운 기술에 대한 공학적 원리를 설명하는 (A), (A)의 마 지막 문장에서 이 새로운 기술이 무게 중심을 낮게 유 지해 줌으로써 더 적은 에너지를 쓰게 한다는 장점을 언급한 뒤 Another advantage로 이어받아 새로운 기술 의 또 다른 장점으로 팔다리가 바에 걸릴 확률이 낮아 진다는 점을 언급한 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 20) ④: (A) 스키 점프 선수들은 공중에서의 시간을 극대화하기 위해 많은 기술을 시도해 왔으며, 초창기의 점프 스타 일은 상체를 곧게 세우는 직립 스타일이었고, 뒤에서 Kongsberger 스타일은 상체를 엉덩이에서 굽혀서 평균 점프 거리를 두 배로 늘렸다고 했으므로 직립 스타일은 Kongsberger 스타일로 ‘대체되었다’는 흐름이 자연스럽 다. 따라서 substituted(대체된)가 적절하다. 본문변형 replaced → substituted precede ~에 선행하다, be preceded by A A보다 뒤에 오다, A가 앞서다 (B) Kongsberger 스타일은 스키를 평행하게 만드는 것 이고, V 스타일은 스키를 V자 모양으로 바꾼 것이므로 이러한 ‘변형‘이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 transformation(변형)이 적절하다. 본문변형 modification → transformation momentum 추진력 (C) 선수들이 더 안전한 속도로 착지할 수 있게 해준다 고 했으므로 부상의 위험을 ’줄인다‘는 흐름이 자연스럽 다. 따라서 mitigate(완화하다)가 적절하다. 본문변형 reducing → mitigate heighten 높이다

(A)
(B)

choices: finding reinvestsimple

solution: (A) marketing strategies에 대한 예시로, 전치사 like(~와 같은) 에 이어지는 동명사구 selecting ~ location이 등위접속사 and 로 병렬 연결되고 있으므로, 동명사 finding이 적절하다. (B) ‘~인지 아닌지’의 의미를 갖는 whether는 뒤에 완전한 절 이 이어지거나 to부정사(구)가 바로 이어질 수 있다. 따라서 주 어 없이 바로 이어지므로 to부정사 to reinvest가 알맞다. Author: Luke Peres
President of The Helpers, the school’s biggest volunteer
club
High school is not only (A)[where / what] we
study different subjects but also where we learn
about life. We are a group of students that get
together every week to discuss ways to make a
difference in our society. In this newsletter, I would
like to share the story of how we participated in
our community’s international food festival. On top
of raising enough money to make a donation, we
learned a lot about how to create and carry out a
business plan. Here is our story.
The first step we took was to decide what to sell.
Some of the ideas that we discussed (B)[to include /
included] cotton candy, corn dogs, and lemonade. Out
of these options, we agreed that a lemonade stand
would be the easiest for us, as we would need only a
good recipe and a few ingredients. We also found out
that no other stand (C)[had / has] signed up to sell
drinks, so lemonade seemed to be the natural choice.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)             (B)
(C)
choices: whereto includehad
whereincludedhad
whereincludedhas
whatincludedhad
whatto includehas
solution: (A) 완전한 절(we ~ subjects)을 이끌어 is의 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으며, 상관접속사 not only A but also B(A뿐 만 아니라 B)에 의해 but also 뒤에 이어지는 선행사 the place 가 생략된 관계부사절 where ~ life와 병렬연결을 이루고 있으므 로, 앞에 선행사 the place가 생략된 관계부사 where가 적절하 다. 참고로, 관계부사 where와 일반 선행사 the place는 둘 중 하나를 생략할 수 있으며, ‘~한 곳(에/에서)’으로 해석할 수 있다. (B) 관계사절의 수식을 받는 주어 Some of the ideas에 대한 동사 자리이므로, 동사 included가 적절하다. (C) 주절의 ‘알게 된’ 과거 시점(found)보다, 어떤 다른 가판대 도 음료 판매를 신청하지 않았다는 것이 더 이전에 일어난 일 이므로 과거완료(had p.p.)시제를 이루는 had가 적절하다.

[1]
Author: Luke Peres
President of The Helpers, the school’s biggest
volunteer club
High school is not only where we study different
subjects but also where we learn about life. We are a
group of students that get together every week to
discuss ways to make a difference in our society. In
this newsletter, I would like to share the story of how
we participated in our community’s international food
festival. On top of raising enough money to make a
donation, we learned a lot about how to create and
carry out a business plan. Here is our story.
[2]
The first step we took was to decide what to sell.
Some of the ideas that we discussed included
cotton candy, corn dogs, and lemonade. Out of
these options, we agreed that a lemonade stand
would be the easiest for us, as we would need only
a good recipe and a few ingredients. We also
found out that no other stand had signed up to
sell drinks, so lemonade seemed to be the natural
choice.
Once we decided on lemonade, we needed the
perfect recipe. Fortunately, we were able to find a
simple one online. We just needed freshly squeezed
lemons, sugar, water, and ice. After trying out
different variations of the recipe on friends and
family, we decided on the final recipe. It would
make about 1.5 liters of lemonade, which could be
sold as five cups.

What to Consider When Making a Business Plan

Planning a Lemonade Stand: Product Choice andRecipe Testing

To stay away from filter bubbles, it is important to
regularly check whether you are already trapped
inside one. One way to do this ⓐis by performing
searches on your favorite online platforms after
logging out. Compare the search results and
recommendations with what you usually see when
you are logged in. If there is a big difference
between them, you ⓑmay have been trapped in a
filter bubble.
ⓒManaging your personal information is another
key to avoiding filter bubbles. ⓓWhenever you go
online, your activities are saved as cookies on your
computer. Websites can collect them based on your
consent. You can remove or limit your consent on
the websites or delete the cookies on your
computer on a regular basis. This way, you can
reduce the amount of personal data ⓔwhat you
unconsciously share as you visit websites. Take
action to break free from your filter bubble and
open yourself up to new ideas.

when she sees her friends’ posts receiving more

Social media is a powerful tool ⓑthat helps us

One of them is ⓒwhat many people place excessive
value on the number of likes and comments they

don’t get enough likes, like Min, may experience
feelings of shame or rejection. This can lead to severe

more popular ones can make them feel inferior and

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

To make social media a positive part of your daily
life, it is important to use it mindfully with some
guidelines. First, don’t let social media consume all
your time and attention. A quick and easy way to
do this is to set limits on your usage or take
regular breaks from social media. This will free up
your time and energy to engage in activities
outside the online world. Second, keep in mind that
social media is a tool to network with others, not a
platform for competition. When you start to feel
unpopular or inferior, remember that what you see
online presents only the highlights of other people’s
lives and does not reflect their entire story. If you
still feel envious, use that emotion as motivation
that helps you with your personal growth. By
following these rules, you can make the most of
social media and feel more at ease in your digital
interactions.

interactions by setting time limits on its use or

remembering that it is for (C)____________ with
others.

(C)

Location-Based Marketing:
When the organizer asked us where we wanted
our stand, we knew that location was going to be
important. She sent us a map showing which foods
were going to be sold at which stands, and we
chose an opening between the tteokbokki and spicy
kebab stands. Who could resist a cool, sweet
lemonade after some spicy and salty food?
Our Marketing Strategies:
Developing marketing strategies to attract more
customers was the most enjoyable part. In addition
to designing posters and fliers, we also explored
various online marketing techniques. One of our
club members suggested we offer customers free
refills for mentioning our stand on their social
media accounts. We all agreed that was a great
way to spread the word. We also planned to install
a photo zone and give coupons for a 10% discount
to customers who posted photos they took there
with the tag “#sweetsuccess,” the name of our stand.
(A) Each club was able to choose the location of
their stand at the festival. (T/F)
(B) The writer thought that people would want to drink
lemonade after eating spicy and salty food. (T/F)
(C) We worked on designing posters and flyers to
attract more customers. (T/F)
(D) The writer suggested offering free refills if customers
mentioned the club’s stand on their social
media accounts. (T/F)
(E) Customers were given a 10% discount coupon
if they took photos of the lemonade and
posted them on social media. (T/F)

of ＄2, we expected a ⓒprofit of ＄1.30 per cup.
Regarding attendance, we learned that the festival
organizers were expecting around 400 people for
each of the two days of the festival. We thought
we could reasonably sell lemonade to half of the
people attending, so we aimed to sell 400 cups
over the two days. If we could do that, our revenue
would amount to ＄800!

needed to ⓓsubtract our costs from it. In addition to
the cost of ＄280 required to make 400 cups, we also
had to ⓔfactor in the ＄6 we needed for posters and
fliers. If we reached our goal, we would be able to
make ＄514 in profit. That would be a big donation!

W: Today, I will share an interesting story from a
power company. Ice storms piled up lots of ice
on power lines, (A)[which / that] caused the
power to go out frequently. (B)[Solve / To solve]
this issue, the power company’s staff gathered
together. During the discussion, someone jokingly
said, “ⓐWhat about training bears in the woods
to shake the electric poles?” Everyone laughed.
Another person said, “We should place jars of
honey at the top of the poles to attract them.”
People laughed even harder. Someone else
added, “We could use helicopters to put the
honey jars on the poles.” Then a woman said,
“Wait. Would (C)[fly / flying] low over the
power lines with a helicopter remove the ice?”
Surprisingly, this last idea became the solution.
A joke about bears led to the innovative idea

legs were too heavy for an open turn, which
caused him to slow down. To overcome this
drawback, he devised a technique that is now
known as a flip turn. He would make a forward roll
first to change direction and then kick against the
wall to speed ahead. This technique allowed him

techniques, such as the scissors and the straddle,
for the Olympics when he was in high school. He
soon realized, however, that these techniques were
challenging for him because he didn’t have the
strength or speed they require. Then he found that
when he went over the bar backward and landed
headfirst, he could jump higher than anyone on his
team. As an engineering major, he later explained
that arching the body backward keeps the jumper’s
center of gravity low to the ground. (A)무게 중심이

body:
Ski jumping is one of the most spectacular winter
Olympic events. The skiers jump from the height of
90 meters, which is as high as a 30-story apartment
building. Most of the skiers are able to stay in the
air for about five to seven seconds. While they are
in the air, they are influenced by “lift,” an upward
force produced by air on a fast-moving object.
When the force of lift is balanced with the force of
gravity, the skiers can fly for long distances. The
key factors for them to increase lift and jumping
distance are increasing their speed, spreading out
their bodies and skis, and adjusting their body angle.
As jumps are judged mostly on jumping distance
as well as their style, skiers have tried many
techniques to maximize their time in the air, aiming
to achieve longer distances. In the beginning, most
skiers simply stood upright throughout their jump.
Later, this upright style was replaced by the
Kongsberger style. The skiers’ upper body was bent
at the hips, with their arms extended in front of
them and their skis parallel to each other. This
technique doubled the average jumping distance.
Everything changed in 1985, however, when Swedish
jumper Jan Boklöv introduced the V style. In this
style, the skiers position their skis into a “V” shape with
their heads placed between the skis. This modification
increases the surface area and creates more lift,
leading to even greater jumping distances. Wind
tunnel tests showed that the V style (A)____________
air lift by 28%, which means that skiers can stay in
the air longer. This style also enables skiers to land
at a safer speed, reducing the risk of injury.
The V style was not immediately adopted by the
skiing community. In fact, it was initially ridiculed
and received fewer style points for breaking the
standard of parallel skis. However, the technique
proved so (B)____________ that by 1992 all Olympic
medalists were using it.

body:
Ski jumping is one of the most spectacular winter
Olympic events. The skiers jump from the height of
90 meters, which is as high as a 30-story apartment
building. Most of the skiers are able to stay in the
air for about five to seven seconds. While they are
in the air, they are influenced by “lift,” an upward
force produced by air on a fast-moving object.
When the force of lift is balanced with the force of
gravity, the skiers can fly for long distances. The
key factors for them to increase lift and jumping
distance are increasing their speed, spreading out
their bodies and skis, and adjusting their body angle.
As jumps are judged mostly on jumping distance
as well as their style, skiers have tried many
techniques to maximize their time in the air, aiming
to achieve longer distances. In the beginning, most
skiers simply stood upright throughout their jump.
Later, this upright style was replaced by the
Kongsberger style. The skiers’ upper body was bent
at the hips, with their arms extended in front of
them and their skis parallel to each other. This
technique doubled the average jumping distance.
Everything changed in 1985, however, when Swedish
jumper Jan Boklöv introduced the V style. In this
style, the skiers position their skis into a “V” shape with
their heads placed between the skis. This modification
increases the surface area and creates more lift,
leading to even greater jumping distances. Wind
tunnel tests showed that the V style (A)____________
air lift by 28%, which means that skiers can stay in
the air longer. This style also enables skiers to land
at a safer speed, reducing the risk of injury.
The V style was not immediately adopted by the
skiing community. In fact, it was initially ridiculed
and received fewer style points for breaking the
standard of parallel skis. However, the technique
proved so (B)____________ that by 1992 all Olympic
medalists were using it.

윗글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: The Most Effective Jumping Style Based on BodyMovement
Scientific Principles of Lift and Gravity Applied inModern Ski Jumping
Fierce Competition Among Professional Skiers toSet New Olympic Records
Continuous Innovations in Ski Jumping TechniquesLeading to a New Standard
The Historical Origins and Development of SkiJumping as an Olympic Event
solution: 스키 점프 선수들은 더 먼 거리를 뛰기 위해 the upright style, Kongsberger style 그리고 the V style과 같은 기술을 발전시켜 왔으며, 처음에는 비판받았던 the V style이 공기 양 력을 높이고 착륙 시 안전성을 확보하는 등 경기력을 향상시 키며 그 결과 1992년에 이르러 모든 올림픽 메달리스트들이 사용하는 새로운 표준이 되었다는 것이 핵심 내용이므로 이 글의 제목으로 적절한 것은 ❹ ‘새로운 기준으로 이어진 스키 점프 기술의 지속적인 혁신’이다.

body:
The Flip Turn in Swimming
Up until the 1936 Olympics, swimmers used an
open turn. They touched the wall with one or two
hands first, turned to the side, and pushed off from
the wall by bending their legs.
(A) He would make a forward roll first to change
direction and then kick against the wall to
speed ahead. This technique allowed him to
maintain as much of his speed and momentum
as possible. His willingness to take a risk and
keep experimenting paid off.
(B) However, open turns had the critical disadvantage
of disrupting the swimmers’ flow and speed. This
problem was resolved by an American high
school student named Al Vande Weghe.
(C) While practicing the backstroke, he realized that
his legs were too heavy for an open turn, which
caused him to slow down. To overcome this
drawback, he devised a technique that is now
known as a flip turn.
Using this technique, he won a silver medal in the
1936 Olympics. Flip turns are now the standard in
freestyle and backstroke races.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 1936년 올림픽까지 사용된 오픈 턴의 방식을 설명하는 주어진 글 뒤에, However(그러나)로 시작해, 앞서 언급된 오픈 턴의 단점을 제시하는 (B), 마지막 문장에서 오픈 턴의 단점을 해결 한 Al Vande Weghe라는 인물을 처음으로 소개하는 (B)에 이 어, Al Vande Weghe를 대명사 he로 이어받아 그가 오픈 턴의 단점을 직접 경험한 구체적인 상황을 설명하고 이러한 결점을 극복하기 위해 현재 플립 턴으로 알려진 기술을 고안했다는 (C), 이 기술에 대해 구체적인 동작 방식과 효과를 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

event without any bottled water? Well, this year,
runners are being provided with a bottleless
drink called Ooho. Ooho is a thin, edible bag
made from seaweed. When filled with water, it
looks like a small water ball. Since the bag itself
is edible, runners can simply eat the whole
thing. If they don’t want to, they can just bite
it, drink the water inside, and then throw the
bag away. The best part? The bag will naturally
break down. (A)In other words, there is no
plastic waste left behind. Ooho will surely
replace the thousands of plastic bottles used
every year during the marathon. Thanks to

towards a greener tomorrow.

body:
In addition to their direct absorption and burial of
CO₂ through whale falls, whales also make a
significant indirect contribution to reducing CO₂
through an act called a whale pump. This refers to
the vertical movements of whales that _______________
________________________________. Whales dive deep into
the ocean to feed on prey such as krill and small
fish, and they occasionally swim up to the surface
to breathe. When they near the surface, they
release an enormous amount of waste. This waste is
rich in nutrients that are essential for creatures
living in that area. Specifically, it creates the perfect
growing conditions for some microscopic creatures
floating at the surface of the ocean.
These creatures, called phytoplankton, may look
tiny and insignificant, but when taken together, they
play a significant role in reducing CO₂. They absorb
about 40% of the carbon in the atmosphere and
produce about 50% of the atmosphere’s oxygen.
They do this through photosynthesis, a process that
creates energy using carbon, water, and light. It is
estimated that increasing the world’s phytoplankton
by 1% is equivalent to planting 2 billion new trees.
Whale pumps deliver nutrients not only to the
ocean surface but also to deeper areas of the
ocean. As whales swim back down to feed at the
ocean’s bottom, their movements stir up the water
and bring nutrients down to the creatures living
below. Whale pumps promote the growth of marine
life at various depths throughout the ocean.
*phytoplankton 식물성 플랑크톤

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: encourage phytoplankton to stay only at thesurface of the sea
decrease the amount of oxygen produced byphytoplankton
help circulate nutrients across different depthsof the ocean
prevent the sunlight from reaching the deep-seacreatures
trap vast amounts of carbon dioxide within the ocean

Whales spread nutrients in the ocean not only
vertically but also horizontally through a process
called the great whale conveyor belt. These giant
mammals migrate over long distances at certain
times of the year. For example, in the summer,
humpback whales tend to stay near Alaska, where
the water is cold but rich in nutrients and prey for
them to feed on. As winter approaches, they travel
up to 4,800 kilometers to breed in the warm waters
near Hawaii.

warm
waters,
which

it
difficult
for

whales arrive in Hawaii after eating their fill in
Alaska, they release a large amount of nutrient-rich
waste. This process can be thought of as a
conveyor belt that moves nutrients from cold waters
to warm waters. These nutrients support the life of
many marine animals and, importantly, encourage
the growth of phytoplankton even in (B)[cold /
warm] waters. The spread of phytoplankton leads to
increased carbon absorption throughout the entire
ocean. Whales circulate water and nutrients to every
corner of the ocean, helping to (C)[foster / combat]
climate change.
(A)
(B)
(C)

과도한 양은 온실 효과의 원인이 되어 왔고, 지구 표면 온도를 점진적으로 상승시키는 결과를 낳았다.”라는 의미이며, 역접을 나타내는 However(하지만)로 시작하므로,이 문장 앞에는 this gas(이 기체)가 적당한 양일 때는심각한 문제를 일으키지 않는다는 내용이 와야 한다.따라서 '이 기체는 일상적인 상황에서는 그 자체로 위험하지 않다'는 문장 있어 첨단 기술과 저차원기술의 해결책의 차이점들16) ③: 고래는 먹이를 먹기 위해 깊은 바다로 잠수했다가 수면으로 올라오며 영양분이 풍부한 배설물을 방출하고, 다시 해저로 내려갈 때는 물을 휘저어 아래에 사는 생물들에게도 영양분을 전달한다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 고래의 수직적 움직임이 바다의 다양한 깊이에 영양분을 순환시킨다는 흐름이 가장 자연스럽다. 따라서빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은 ③ ‘바다의 서로 다른깊이로 영양분을 순환시키도록 돕는다‘이다.오답① 식물성 플랑크톤이 바다 표면에만 머물도록 장려한다② 식물성 플랑크톤에 의해 생산되는 산소의 양을 감소시킨다④ 햇빛이 심해 생물들에게 도달하는 것을 막는다⑤ 바다 내부에 방대한 양의 이산화탄소를 가둔다17) vertical, surface, 하와이에 도착하면 영양분이 풍부한 상당량의 배설물을배출한다고 했으므로, 이 영양분들이 따뜻한 바다에서조차도 식물성 플랑크톤의 성장을 촉진한다는 흐름이자연스럽다. 따라서 warm(따뜻한)이 적절하다.cold 차가운(C) 앞에서 식물성 플랑크톤의 확산이 해양 전체에 걸쳐 탄소 흡수를 증가시킨다고 했으므로 고래가 바다구석구석에 영양분을 순환시켜 기후 변화에 맞서 W: Welcome, everyone! Today, I want to give you
some essential tips on online safety. It’s crucial
to protect your personal information while
enjoying the internet. First, always use strong
passwords for your online accounts. Choose
complex passwords (A)[that / what] include a
mix of letters, numbers, and special characters.
Avoid information others can easily guess, such
as your date of birth or pet’s name. Secondly,
pay attention to your privacy settings on social
media. Adjust (B)[who / how] can see your
posts and personal information. It’s important to
be cautious when (C)[sharing / shared] personal
details with online friends. By following these
two simple but critical tips, you can enjoy the
internet safely. Remember, your online safety is
in your own hands.

위 담화의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)              (B)
(C)
choices: that   whosharing
that   howshared
what   whosharing
that   whoshared
what   howsharing
solution: (A) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(include ~ characters)을 이끌어 선행사 complex passwords를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. (B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can see ~ information)을 이끌어 동사 Adjust의 목적어 역할을 하는 간접의문문을 이루는 의문 사 자리이며 동시에 간접의문문의 주어 역할을 해야 하므로 의문대명사 who가 적절하다. (C) 부사절 접속사 when 뒤에 주어와 동사가 없으므로 접속사를 생략하지 않은 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어 인 you가 ‘공유하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어 personal details가 이어지므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 sharing이 적절하다.

Avoid Copyright Violations
Cathy is an ⓐenthusiastic gamer who shares her
gameplays on a popular video-sharing platform.
Recently,
her
channel

for

Cathy’s mistake is not uncommon in the content
creation community. Creators often miss embedded
copyrighted material, such as background music,
sound effects, images, and video clips. Even a brief
appearance of such material can put creators at risk
of a copyright claim.
To avoid any potential copyright issues, creators
should research their creation to check if any of its
components are copyrighted. If they come across
copyrighted content, they should contact the copyright
owner for permission to use it, replace it with
non-copyrighted material, or remove it completely.
ⓓUtilizing material with a Creative Commons (CC)
license might also be a good idea. Most of this
material can be used at no cost as long as certain
rules are ⓔfollowed. These simple steps can help
content creators avoid unexpected copyright issues
and have some peace of mind about their work.

and excitement about something
ⓑ suspend: to officially stop something from continuing,
especially for a short time
ⓒ violation: an action that causes harm or damage
by treating someone or their possessions
without respect
ⓓ utilize: to use something for a particular purpose
ⓔ follow: to do the same thing as someone else

photos every day and enjoys getting likes and
comments. Lately, however, she began to be
concerned about her social media activity. She
realizes that she spends a considerable amount of
time repeatedly checking her feed, desperately
seeking more likes. She even feels disappointed
when she sees her friends’ posts (A)[receiving /
received] more likes than hers.
Social media is a powerful tool that helps us
connect with others, but it also has its downsides.
One of them is that many people place excessive
value on the number of likes and comments
(B)[that / what] they get on their posts. Those who
feel that they don’t get enough likes, like Min, may
ⓐ_______________________________________________________.

make them feel (C)[inferior / inferiorly] and harm

(A)
(B)           (C)
choices: received    thatinferior
receiving    thatinferiorly

solution: (A) 지각동사로 쓰인 sees와 목적어 her friends’ posts에 이어 진 목적격보어 자리로, 지각동사는 목적어와 목적격보어의 관 계가 능동일 때 목적격보어로 동사원형 또는 진행을 강조하는 현재분사를 사용하고, 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 수동일 때 목적격보어로 과거분사를 사용한다. 따라서 목적어 her friends’ posts가 ‘받는’ 주체이므로, 능동의 의미이자 진행의 의 미를 강조하는 현재분사 receiving이 적절하다. from a website whose domain ends with “.net,”
ⓐwhat means it’s a private site. On the other hand,

octopuses are endangered because wealthy people

sound ⓒreasonably. Meanwhile, the bird story

speaking more than two languages. Lastly, check if

To make social media a positive part of your daily
life, it is important to use it mindfully with some
guidelines. First, don’t let social media ⓐ[consume /
to consume] all your time and attention. A quick
and easy way to do this is to set limits on your
usage or ⓑ[takes / take] regular breaks from social
media. This will (A)____________ your time and energy
to engage in activities outside the online world.
Second, keep in mind that social media is a tool to
network with others, not a platform for competition.
When you start to feel unpopular or inferior,
remember that what you see online presents only
the highlights of other people’s lives and does not
reflect their (B)___________ story. If you still feel envious,
use that emotion as motivation ⓒ[what / that]
helps you with your personal growth. By following
these rules, you can make the most of social media
and feel more at ease in your digital interactions.

body:
Cathy is an enthusiastic gamer who shares her
gameplays on a popular video-sharing platform.
Recently, her channel was suspended for copyright
violation issues. She was shocked to learn that the
background music played within the game had a
copyright claim. Now Cathy wants to know how to
avoid similar issues in the future.
Cathy’s mistake is not uncommon in the content
creation community. Creators often miss embedded
copyrighted material, such as background music,
sound effects, images, and video clips. Even a brief
appearance of such material can put creators at risk
of a copyright claim.
To avoid any potential copyright issues, creators
should research their creation to check if any of its
components are copyrighted. If they come across
copyrighted
content,
they
should
contact
the
copyright owner for permission to use it, replaced it
with
non-copyrighted
material,
or
remove
it
completely.
Utilizing
material
with
a
Creative
Commons (CC) license might also be a good idea.
Most of this material can be used at no cost as
long as certain rules are followed. These simple
steps can help content creators avoid unexpected
copyright issues and have some peace of mind
about their work.
CREATIVE COMMONS (CC) LICENSE TERMS
BY (Attribution)
Credit must be give to the creator.
NC (Non-Commercial)
Only non-commercial uses of the work are permitted.
ND (No Derivatives)
No derivatives or adaptations of the work are
permitted.
SA (Share Alike)
Adaptation must be shared under the same license
as the original.

or에 의해 병렬 연결된 2형식 동사 look과 sound 뒤에 이어지는 공통의 주격보어 자리이므로, 부사 reasonably를 형용사 reasonable 로 고친다.) 오답 ⓑ 완전한 절(tree ~ endangered)을 이끌어 동사 claims 의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다. ⓓ 선행사 므로 복수로 수일치한 복수동사 are는 적절하다. 2) ⑤: 새 이야기는 두 개 이상의 언어를 구사하는 앵무새들의 증 거를 제공하는 연구들을 제시하며, 또한 앵무새의 언어 능 력에 대해 더 많은 연구들이 있다고 했으므로 ⑤ ‘두 가지 언어를 말하는 앵무새에 관한 이야기는 추가적인 증거가 부족하므로 가짜 뉴스로 판별된다.’는 일치하지 않는 내 용이다. 오답 그 정보는 신뢰할 수 있다고 볼 수 있다. 3) ①, ② : 필자는 독자들에게 온라인 콘텐츠의 저작권 문제, 온라인 쇼핑 추천에 과도하게 영향받는 문제, 소셜 미디어에서 ‘좋 아요’와 댓글에 집착하는 문제에 대해 질문을 던진 뒤, 독 자들이 더 건강한 디지털 생활을 할 수 있도록 도와줄 몇 가지 조언과 아이디어가 있다고 하며 글을 마무리하고 있 다. 따라서
